sources.entry: openpyxl - A library for reading and writing Excel 2010 xlsx/xlsm/xltx/xltm files.

summary.name: openpyxl
summary.one_liner: openpyxl is an MIT-licensed Python library for reading and writing Excel 2010 xlsx/xlsm/xltx/xltm files.
use_cases: Reading data from Excel files in Python
Generating xlsx reports from Python scripts
Writing cell values and rows to spreadsheets
summary.what_it_does: The library reads and writes Excel 2010 xlsx, xlsm, xltx and xltm files natively from Python, using the Office Open XML format. Its sample code shows creating a workbook, getting the active worksheet, assigning values to cells, appending rows, and saving to a file. Python types such as datetime are converted automatically when written to cells. The page links to documentation, release notes, and a contributor guide, and notes it was originally based on PHPExcel.
notable: Reads and writes xlsx, xlsm, xltx and xltm Excel 2010 files natively in Python
Automatic conversion of Python types such as datetime when writing cells
Optional defusedxml install to guard against XML attacks
caveats: By default does not guard against quadratic blowup or billion laughs XML attacks; install defusedxml for protection
Maintained by volunteers in spare time, so some features may be missing
Page lists supported Python versions as 3.6 to 3.9, which may be outdated relative to the stated version 3.1.3
